```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6, dpi = 110)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2))

# ---- Constants (edit here) ----------------------------------------------
DATA  <- "../data"     # committed tidy tables, relative to this notebook
ALPHA <- 0.05          # nominal level (dotted reference line)

# Validated reference categorical palette; the gamma encoding matches
# aggregators/plot_thesis_power.R (blue circle 0, aqua triangle 0.25,
# yellow square 0.45) so every figure in the repo reads the same way.
COL1 <- "#2a78d6"; COL2 <- "#1baf7a"; COL3 <- "#eda100"; COL4 <- "#eb6834"
INK_PRIMARY <- "#0b0b0b"; INK_SECONDARY <- "#52514e"; INK_MUTED <- "#898781"
GRIDLINE <- "#e1e0d9"

gamma_cols   <- c(`0` = COL1, `0.25` = COL2, `0.45` = COL3)
gamma_shapes <- c(`0` = 16, `0.25` = 17, `0.45` = 15)
gamma_labels <- c(expression(gamma == 0), expression(gamma == 0.25),
                  expression(gamma == 0.45))
scale_gamma <- list(
  scale_colour_manual(values = gamma_cols, labels = gamma_labels, name = NULL),
  scale_shape_manual(values = gamma_shapes, labels = gamma_labels, name = NULL),
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)))

theme_grid <- theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  theme(legend.position  = "bottom",
        legend.text      = element_text(size = 12, colour = INK_PRIMARY),
        axis.title       = element_text(size = 12, colour = INK_SECONDARY),
        axis.text        = element_text(size = 9, colour = INK_MUTED),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 11, colour = INK_PRIMARY,
                                        face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = GRIDLINE, linewidth = 0.4),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing    = unit(0.7, "lines"))

F_LABELS <- c(F1 = "F1: N(0,1) vs Pa(a)", F2 = "F2: Pa(1.5) vs Pa(a)",
              F3 = "F3: random walk, Pa(a)", F4 = "F4: FAR(1) epidemic")
S_LABELS <- c(S1 = "S1: mean shift", S2 = "S2: noncentr. chi-sq",
              S3 = "S3: Pareto scale", S4 = "S4: Beta shape",
              S5 = "S5: Pareto shape")
PROJ_LEVELS <- c("ito", "l2", "c_max_var")
```

Every figure below is drawn from a committed tidy table in
`reproduction/data/`; the section text names the script that regenerates
each table, so the plots never depend on rerunning the multi-hour sweeps.
Provenance matters here: the thesis power section shows the
dissertation's record as printed (assembled from the thesis tables, with
the F1/F2 cells rerun at N_rep = 100), produced by the legacy research
implementations, while the F5, calibration and audit sections use the
corrected statistic family. The last section visualizes exactly what the
correction changes. The static figure versions with the full long/short
segment grids are produced by `aggregators/plot_thesis_power.R`.

## The thesis power study

`data/thesis_power_values.csv` is the tidy assembly of the dissertation's
power tables (built by `aggregators/assemble_thesis_power.R`; the `source`
column records the provenance of every row). Layout shared by the three
functional figures: columns are the scenarios F1 to F4, rows the
projections, lines the weight exponent gamma, and the dotted line the
nominal level. Long-segment results (`l* = n/5`) are shown; the short
segment (`l* = [log n] + 1`) tells the same story with less power and is
in the static figures.

```{r power-data}
dat <- read.csv(file.path(DATA, "thesis_power_values.csv"))
dat$g <- factor(dat$gamma, levels = c(0, 0.25, 0.45))

functional_fig <- function(test_id, proj_labels, subtitle) {
  d <- dat[dat$test == test_id & dat$scenario %in% names(F_LABELS) &
           dat$segment == "long" & (is.na(dat$m) | dat$m == 1), ]
  d$sc_lab   <- factor(d$scenario, names(F_LABELS), F_LABELS)
  d$proj_lab <- factor(d$projection, PROJ_LEVELS, proj_labels)
  ggplot(d, aes(a, power, colour = g, shape = g)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = ALPHA, linetype = "dotted", colour = INK_MUTED) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
    facet_grid(proj_lab ~ sc_lab, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_gamma +
    labs(x = "change magnitude a", y = "rejection rate",
         subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_grid
}
proj_plain <- c("Ito projection", "L2 norm", "C max-var")
proj_rkhs  <- c("Ito + Gaussian", "L2 + min", "C max-var + Gaussian")
```

### Wilcoxon scan (h_0 kernel, m = 1)

```{r power-wilcoxon}
functional_fig("wilcoxon", proj_plain, "Wilcoxon scan, long segment")
```

### Lp scan (p = 2)

```{r power-lp}
functional_fig("lp", proj_plain, "Lp scan, long segment")
```

### RKHS scan (rank-calibrated)

F4 uses the FAR(1) finite-sample null.

```{r power-rkhs}
functional_fig("rkhs", proj_rkhs, "RKHS scan, long segment")
```

### The scalar scenarios

The RKHS row shows the matched kernel per scenario; the S3/S5 panels are
empty because no Pareto-baseline null cache is shipped, the same gap as
in the printed thesis.

```{r power-scalar, fig.height = 5.6}
d <- dat[dat$scenario %in% names(S_LABELS) & dat$segment == "long" &
         ((dat$test == "wilcoxon" & dat$m == 1) | dat$test %in% c("lp", "rkhs")), ]
test_labels <- c(wilcoxon = "Wilcoxon m=1", lp = "Lp p=2", rkhs = "RKHS matched")
d$test_lab <- factor(test_labels[d$test], test_labels)
d$sc_lab   <- factor(d$scenario, names(S_LABELS), S_LABELS)
ggplot(d, aes(a, power, colour = g, shape = g)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ALPHA, linetype = "dotted", colour = INK_MUTED) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  facet_grid(test_lab ~ sc_lab) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "sqrt", breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8)) +
  scale_gamma +
  labs(x = "change magnitude a", y = "rejection rate",
       subtitle = "Scalar scenarios, long segment") +
  theme_grid
```

### F4 cross-method, including the FAR(1) statistic

The scan tests are shown at the L2-norm projection (the
thesis-highlighted pairing); the Birbilas-type `far1` statistic consumes
the curves directly.

```{r power-f4, fig.height = 4.8}
d <- dat[dat$scenario == "F4" &
         ((dat$test == "wilcoxon" & dat$projection == "l2" & dat$m == 1) |
          (dat$test %in% c("lp", "rkhs") & dat$projection == "l2") |
          (dat$test == "far1")), ]
m_labels <- c(wilcoxon = "Wilcoxon (h_0, m = 1)", lp = "Lp (p = 2)",
              rkhs = "RKHS (min)", far1 = "Birbilas E (adj. CV)")
d$m_lab   <- factor(m_labels[d$test], m_labels)
d$seg_lab <- factor(d$segment, c("long", "short"),
                    c("long segment", "short segment"))
ggplot(d, aes(a, power, colour = g, shape = g)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ALPHA, linetype = "dotted", colour = INK_MUTED) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  facet_grid(seg_lab ~ m_lab) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "sqrt", breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8)) +
  scale_gamma +
  labs(x = "change magnitude a", y = "rejection rate",
       subtitle = "F4: FAR(1) epidemic mean change") +
  theme_grid
```

### The splitting parameter m

Paper 1's split statistic `T^(d)` divides the sample into m chunks,
redraws the (stochastic) projection per chunk, and takes the outer
maximum; `scan_over_splits()` implements it. The printed record covers
m in {1, 2, 4} for the Wilcoxon scan: the full scalar grids and the
F3/F4 functional grids (all three projections; l2 shown below), while
for F1/F2 only the l2 strip at gamma = 0 survives.

```{r m-scalar, fig.height = 5.6}
dm <- dat[dat$test == "wilcoxon" & dat$scenario %in% names(S_LABELS) &
          dat$segment == "long", ]
dm$m_lab  <- factor(dm$m, c(1, 2, 4), paste("m =", c(1, 2, 4)))
dm$sc_lab <- factor(dm$scenario, names(S_LABELS), S_LABELS)
ggplot(dm, aes(a, power, colour = g, shape = g)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ALPHA, linetype = "dotted", colour = INK_MUTED) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  facet_grid(m_lab ~ sc_lab) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "sqrt", breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8)) +
  scale_gamma +
  labs(x = "change magnitude a", y = "rejection rate",
       subtitle = "Wilcoxon scan over splits, scalar scenarios, long segment") +
  theme_grid
```

```{r m-functional, fig.height = 5.2}
df <- dat[dat$test == "wilcoxon" & dat$scenario %in% c("F3", "F4") &
          dat$segment == "long" & dat$projection == "l2", ]
df$m_lab  <- factor(df$m, c(1, 2, 4), paste("m =", c(1, 2, 4)))
df$sc_lab <- factor(df$scenario, c("F3", "F4"), F_LABELS[c("F3", "F4")])
ggplot(df, aes(a, power, colour = g, shape = g)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ALPHA, linetype = "dotted", colour = INK_MUTED) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  facet_grid(m_lab ~ sc_lab, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_gamma +
  labs(x = "change magnitude a", y = "rejection rate",
       subtitle = "Wilcoxon over splits, F3/F4 at the L2-norm projection, long segment") +
  theme_grid
```

```{r m-strip, fig.height = 3.6}
wm <- dat[dat$test == "wilcoxon" & dat$scenario %in% c("F1", "F2") &
          dat$segment == "long" & dat$projection == "l2" & dat$gamma == 0, ]
wm$sc_lab <- factor(wm$scenario, c("F1", "F2"), F_LABELS[c("F1", "F2")])
wm$m <- factor(wm$m)
ggplot(wm, aes(a, power, colour = m, shape = m)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ALPHA, linetype = "dotted", colour = INK_MUTED) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) + geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ sc_lab, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`1` = COL1, `2` = COL2, `4` = COL3),
                      name = "splits m") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`1` = 16, `2` = 17, `4` = 15),
                     name = "splits m") +
  labs(x = "Pareto tail index a", y = "rejection rate",
       subtitle = "The preserved F1/F2 evidence: l2 projection, gamma = 0, long segment") +
  theme_grid
```

The record's verdict: splitting costs power on these designs. m = 1 has
the best mean power everywhere (scalar long segment: 0.47 vs 0.29 at
m = 2 and 0.34 at m = 4; F3/F4 show the same ordering at every
projection), because each chunk sees a shorter sample and the change
window can straddle chunk boundaries. m = 4 consistently recovers part
of m = 2's loss - more chunks mean more chances that one chunk isolates
the window with a fresh projection draw. These are printed (legacy
family) values, so the m comparison is internally consistent, but the
gamma = 0.45 rows inherit the weight defect shown in the audit section.

## The restored F5 spike study

`data/f5_spike_power.csv` (regenerate with
`sweeps/run_f5_spike_power.sh`; n = 400, N_rep = 100) is the experiment
behind the thesis's claim that point-evaluation projections suit
spike-type changes. F5 adds `a * f_alpha(t)` to i.i.d. Wiener curves on
the change window; the study runs the standard long window and a narrow
one covering only the spike's neighbourhood.

```{r f5-spike, fig.height = 5}
f5 <- read.csv(file.path(DATA, "f5_spike_power.csv"))
f5$g <- factor(f5$gamma, levels = c(0, 0.25, 0.45))
f5$proj_lab <- factor(f5$projection, PROJ_LEVELS, proj_plain)
f5$m_lab <- factor(f5$method, c("wilcoxon", "lp"),
                   c("Wilcoxon (h_0)", "Lp (p = 2)"))
f5$seg <- factor(f5$ec_length, c(0.2, 0.015),
                 c("long window (0.4, 0.6)", "narrow window (l/n = 0.015)"))
ggplot(f5, aes(a, power, colour = g, shape = g, linetype = seg)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ALPHA, linetype = "dotted", colour = INK_MUTED) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  facet_grid(m_lab ~ proj_lab) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "sqrt", breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 4, 10)) +
  scale_gamma +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "42"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "spike amplitude a", y = "rejection rate",
       subtitle = "F5: Wiener curves + f_alpha spike") +
  theme_grid
```

The verdict is nuanced, and the figure shows it: the point-evaluation
projection `c_max_var` is the most powerful for faint spikes (for the Lp
scan at a = 0.5 to 1 it reaches 2 to 3 times the power of `l2`) and has
the best mean power overall for Lp, but it is not uniformly dominant. At
large amplitudes the norm projections catch up, and for the Wilcoxon h_0
scan `l2` wins on average.

## The Lp exponent p

The thesis printed the Lp scan at p = 2 only. `data/lp_p_power.csv`
(regenerate with `sweeps/run_lp_p_study.sh`, then
`aggregators/aggregate_lp_p.R`) extends the scalar grid to p in
{2, 4, 10} - all three runs use the **corrected** family on identical
seeds (n = 400, N_rep = 100), so unlike the printed scalar figure above
this is a like-for-like comparison, not the legacy record.

```{r lp-p, fig.height = 5.6}
pp <- read.csv(file.path(DATA, "lp_p_power.csv"))
pp$g <- factor(pp$gamma, levels = c(0, 0.25, 0.45))
pp$p_lab  <- factor(pp$p, c(2, 4, 10), paste("p =", c(2, 4, 10)))
pp$sc_lab <- factor(pp$scenario, names(S_LABELS), S_LABELS)
lp_p_fig <- function(d, subtitle) {
  ggplot(d, aes(a, power, colour = g, shape = g)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = ALPHA, linetype = "dotted", colour = INK_MUTED) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
    facet_grid(p_lab ~ sc_lab) +
    scale_x_continuous(trans = "sqrt", breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 4, 8)) +
    scale_gamma +
    labs(x = "change magnitude a", y = "rejection rate",
         subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_grid
}
lp_p_fig(pp[pp$ec_length == 0.2, ],
         "Corrected Lp scan, scalar scenarios, long segment (l = n/5)")
```

```{r lp-p-short, fig.height = 5.6}
lp_p_fig(pp[pp$ec_length == 0.015, ],
         "The same grid on the short segment (l = floor(log n) + 1 = 6)")
```

The verdict: the exponent barely matters where the test has power. On
the long segment p = 2 and p = 4 are within Monte-Carlo noise of each
other in every cell, and p = 10 trails by a few points at most. The
short segment separates them: at gamma = 0.25 the p = 10 scan loses
roughly two thirds of its (already small) power (mean 0.05 to 0.07
over the alternatives, vs 0.13 to 0.18 for p = 2 and 4), while at
gamma = 0.45, the right weight for short windows, p = 2 and p = 4
remain indistinguishable and p = 10 trails modestly, most visibly on
S5's heavy tails. Empirical size sits near the nominal level throughout (worst
cells 0.11 to 0.13, about three binomial standard errors at
N_rep = 100). Nothing here rewards an exponent above the thesis's
p = 2 default.

## Asymptotic vs finite-sample calibration

`data/mc_calibration_demo.csv` (regenerate with
`mc_calibration_demo.R`) compares the asymptotic critical values with
finite-n Monte-Carlo ones on S1. Two different stories in one figure: the
asymptotic Wilcoxon cv is mildly conservative (size 0.01 to 0.03, some
power lost at n = 100), while the asymptotic Lp cv is badly anticonservative
at gamma 0 and 0.25 (size 0.25 to 0.41, not shrinking with n; this is the
size problem visible in the printed thesis Lp tables). Finite-n
Monte-Carlo calibration puts both tests on the nominal level; the Lp
power cells were not part of this demo run, hence the empty panel.

```{r calibration, fig.height = 4.2}
mc <- read.csv(file.path(DATA, "mc_calibration_demo.csv"))
long <- rbind(
  data.frame(mc[c("test", "n", "gamma")], what = "size",
             calibration = "asymptotic", value = mc$size_asym),
  data.frame(mc[c("test", "n", "gamma")], what = "size",
             calibration = "finite-n MC", value = mc$size_mc),
  data.frame(mc[c("test", "n", "gamma")], what = "power (a = 1)",
             calibration = "asymptotic", value = mc$power_asym),
  data.frame(mc[c("test", "n", "gamma")], what = "power (a = 1)",
             calibration = "finite-n MC", value = mc$power_mc))
long$g <- factor(long$gamma, levels = c(0, 0.25, 0.45))
long$test_lab <- factor(long$test, c("wilcoxon", "lp"),
                        c("Wilcoxon", "Lp (p = 2)"))
ggplot(long, aes(n, value, colour = g, shape = g, linetype = calibration)) +
  geom_hline(data = data.frame(what = "size", y = ALPHA),
             aes(yintercept = y), linetype = "dotted", colour = INK_MUTED) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  facet_grid(what ~ test_lab, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = gamma_cols, labels = gamma_labels, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = gamma_shapes, labels = gamma_labels, name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(asymptotic = "22", `finite-n MC` = "solid"),
                        name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(100, 200, 400)) +
  labs(x = "sample size n", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "S1 mean shift: asymptotic vs finite-n Monte-Carlo calibration") +
  theme_grid
```

## What the statistic audit changed

`data/corrected_vs_legacy.csv` (regenerate with
`compare_exact_vs_legacy.R`, `FAMILY = "corrected"`) reruns the full
power grid with the legacy research implementations and the corrected
family on identical seeds. Points above the diagonal gained power from
the correction. The Wilcoxon panel is the headline: the legacy code
inverted the Hoelder weight, which destroyed its power at gamma > 0, so
the corrected scan dominates there (the column of points at legacy power
zero) while the gamma = 0 points sit near the diagonal. Lp and RKHS move
in both directions because the correction also changes their null
calibration, so some cells lose nominal-level-inflated "power"; far1
barely moves.

```{r audit, fig.height = 4.4}
cl <- read.csv(file.path(DATA, "corrected_vs_legacy.csv"))
cl$g <- factor(cl$gamma, levels = c(0, 0.25, 0.45))
cl$m_lab <- factor(cl$method, c("wilcoxon", "lp", "rkhs", "far1"),
                   c("Wilcoxon", "Lp", "RKHS", "far1"))
ggplot(cl, aes(power_legacy, power_new, colour = g)) +
  geom_abline(colour = INK_MUTED, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_point(size = 1.1, alpha = 0.55) +
  facet_wrap(~ m_lab, nrow = 1) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = gamma_cols, labels = gamma_labels, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "power, legacy implementation", y = "power, corrected family",
       subtitle = "Same seeds, both implementations, full grid") +
  theme_grid + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The companion `data/corrected_vs_legacy_stability.csv` repeats the
comparison over independent seeds to separate genuine differences from
Monte-Carlo noise; `data/exact_vs_legacy.csv` documents that the package
equals the audited original code exactly where no defect was corrected.
